whatItDoes: Allow the school district to borrow $1.35 million through bonds, with total repayment of up to $2.36 million and property taxes of up to $120,000 a year to repay them. Borrowing could occur only if the district receives more than $23 million in BEST grant funds that do not have to be repaid. The money would improve and equip school facilities.
yesMeans: Authorize the bonds and repayment taxes, subject to receiving the required BEST grant and the stated dollar limits.
noMeans: Reject this proposed bond debt and its repayment taxes.

parts.label: Facility projects
parts.what: Projects would include expanding the main building to put all classrooms inside it; replacing old sewer infrastructure; building an auxiliary gym and vocational-agriculture shop; and upgrading the main gym, kitchen, locker rooms and science classroom.

parts.label: Bond and tax terms
parts.what: The school board would set the bonds’ timing, interest, maturity and redemption terms, including any redemption premium, and could sell them at, above or below face value. The property-tax rate would have no fixed mill-rate ceiling, but collections would remain subject to the dollar limits in the question.
